body:
Quake chooses the land around Pristinia as home and repeatedly works to keep it habitable: scouting, training volunteers, moving earth and returning when another threat appears. His own death and the ruined figure he later encounters complicate that duty. He keeps learning, accepts rescue and eventually argues that survival may require leaving a fight.

The first wave · March 2024

Within two days of arrival, Quake joins the reconnaissance west of Pristinia that spots something of island-like scale moving in the distance. Quake then helps answer the Weary Traveler’s request to find missing friends and participates as Melian divides the newcomers among militia planning, medical work, material searches, and surveys of usable land.

Quake takes part in exploration and government while both are still being improvised; the same people who investigate the unknown must decide how a town trains defenders, treats injuries, and uses land.

Building and defending Pristinia

Quake helps drill Pristinia’s volunteers, responds to the dying messenger from Eovar, and works beside the crews raising the treated-log palisade, staked moat, and first watchtowers. Quake also participates in the accord with Cigal’s wolves, choosing negotiated protection of the farms over extermination.

On 27 April, with Rolen gone and the Travelers absent, Quake stands among the remaining adventurers and townsfolk who finish Pristinia’s defenses and repel an attack.

The staff and the coastal ritual

On 18 May, Quake’s corrupted-radiant staff points the company toward rival beacons at a reality-splitting ritual on Prima’s coast. The party stops the ritual, but its last-minute destruction buries most of the evidence. The staff is therefore both instrument and unresolved clue: useful enough to locate a threat, strange enough that its own history still requires recovery.

Quake believes that both he and the staff need purification. He holds it while inviting the others to touch it and see the direction it shows, and presses the company to travel north. At the fork between light and darkness he asks them to choose.

His later report keeps the human cost of that choice visible. He says he took the wrong path, that captives were sacrificed before they arrived and that the company only just stopped the summoning. Stopping the ritual does not turn his account into an uncomplicated rescue. His judgment of his own failure remains beside the destruction of the evidence.

Relationships carried through action

  • Elenia and Nienna: Quake’s earlier rescue becomes Elenia’s reason for using Death Ward, preserving a debt as active care rather than sentiment.
  • Gartina: the regional map confirms a shared Gartina and Quake Estate, though the personal and civic history behind the name remains unrecovered.
  • Pristinia: scouting, rescue, militia work, construction, negotiation, and defense make the settlement itself one of Quake’s longest relationships.
  • Wrath: when Wrath offers grieving adventurers a path through Death after Dale’s fall, Quake refuses before the party fully understands the bargain’s danger.

The open record

Quake describes an upbringing in a hard-working society, study of the land’s magic, an earlier death and the rescue that preceded it. The full pre-Calling biography, original rescue sequence and every step of his return remain incompletely recovered.

The valley encounter and Nuleah’s gift now establish more of the young staff’s history. Its full properties, the complete cause of Quake’s condition and the outcome of the promised purification research remain open. The shared farmland is also named in direct conversation with Gartina, without supplying their complete personal or property history.

His later participation in the assault on Wrath extends the earlier selection that ended in the Month of Cala, Year 1. Neither the burial request nor his absence from still later selected scenes establishes a final death or permanent disappearance.

Contemporary reputation · 20 April 2024

Ada remembers Quake through sacrifice, reincarnation, farming with Gartina, militia training, and defense. The chronicle is evidence that Pristinia understood Quake as both supernatural survivor and builder of local continuity; direct records still govern the exact mechanics of those events. Read the chronicler’s evidence boundary.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2024-05-19 · quest

    A rescue remembered through failure

    Quake tells Dale that he and others died trying to rescue an ambushed company, while others succeeded.

    Known at this stage
    He speaks from a later memory of the rescue.
    Consequence
    His own account gives credit beyond himself and makes failure part of his history.
    Still unresolved
    The speech is not a complete casualty list or a reconstruction of each rescue action.

    Receipt 1

  2. 2024-06-12 · quest

    A duty beyond defeating an enemy

    Quake answers that their duty is to protect the land and its people.

    Known at this stage
    The company is discussing the burden of the watch.
    Consequence
    His stated obligation reaches beyond a single battle.
    Still unresolved

    Receipt 1

  3. 2024-07-19 · quest

    Receiving protection in return

    Elenia protects Quake with Death Ward, recalling earlier survival with Nienna; he thanks her.

    Known at this stage
    The spell is preparation for danger.
    Consequence
    Mutual protection links his history to Elenia’s learning.
    Still unresolved
    The protection is not a guarantee of survival or an explanation of every later return.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

Choosing a home, and learning to keep it

Within the first days of arrival, Quake says he chose to come and that this land is now his home. His fist-to-chest salute accompanies a promise to protect it and its people. It is a commitment he makes before the defenses, institutions and shared knowledge are secure.

During the construction work he tells Elenia about the society he came from: the land gave little, everyone had to work and he studied its magic in what spare time remained. Access to Pristinia’s library has allowed him to learn more. The account explains why labor and study sit so easily beside fighting in his days, without recovering the name or whole history of his former home.

He gives the militia recruits criticism over drinks after a practice fight, watches from the completed tower and calls it a good day. He can also offer a mundane solution to a foul smell—scent the upper lip with peppermint or tea tree. His repeated attention to the land includes people trying to get through an unpleasant day.

The valley and the face he left behind

At the Tree, Quake hears Nuleah warn that crossing the boundary of death can attract dangerous attention. He says his own soul has made that journey, looks at his red hands and keeps his distance from the light. Nuleah’s explanation remains her account of the danger; the scene establishes Quake’s recognition of it and the caution that follows.

In the valley a ruined Earth Genasi confronts him, asking whether Quake thought he could leave him behind. The narrator describes Death’s magic around the figure. Quake advances with his shield, answers that protecting the land is his duty and fights what he later calls a shade of his former self.

The company’s victory is costly. As the shade falls, Quake collapses and the undead forming under its supervision begin to crumble. Bitoshi rushes to the fallen with healing berries; the narrator confirms that everyone is up again. The recovered sequence gives Bitoshi an actual rescue, and Quake a battle in which conviction did not keep him standing.

Nuleah still denies him access to the Tree while calling him impure. She gives him a fresh young staff and says the scholars will look for magic that may purify his soul. Those are a gift and a promise to investigate. They do not establish that his condition is cured, that the shade can never return or that every death and change of body has been fully explained.

A route to Gael, and a vote to leave

The staff stays with Quake on the moving island journeys. He places it in the altar, retrieves it when the company needs to leave and runs to catch the ship. At the helm he helps keep the wheel under control. The scenes show repeated use of a learned route, while Quake can still admit that he does not know the destination.

On Gael he warns that the land beyond the Temple remains dangerous and calls for the removal of Death’s influence. He wants the party to bring back material for study and grow stronger. He also refuses to help use undeath, which he regards as the enemy’s power. That is his stated boundary, not a settled verdict on every companion who understands shadow or death differently.

Inside Vysaeth’s tomb, he hopes the old civilization has left something the company can use. When that hope runs into the risk of Wrath breaking in, he weighs sealing passages, leaving and returning later. He calls for a vote, warning that every delay increases the danger. During the escape he urges them to fight only enough to run.

The defender who repeatedly promises to stand his ground can also argue for withdrawal. His proposal to close an entrance is not proof of a permanently sealed tomb.

Wrath, a burial request and a refused peace

Quake remains with the company in the later assault on Wrath. When Gartina comes to help him and promises that they will see their farmland again, he asks to be buried beside his planted staff. The exchange confirms a shared place they want to return to and the fear that he may not reach it. It does not establish that he dies there.

He continues. Approaching the inner defenses, he warns the others not to be afraid and takes on Wrath’s appearance with the crown. The disguise is something he attempts in the assault; it does not make him Wrath or prove that every enemy is deceived.

After Saray kills Wrath, Quake hears Death’s offer and rejects its hollow peace. He believes mortal strength may one day surpass the gods and allow people to choose the world they want. That is his hope for the future, not a battle already won.

As Draygar, Saray, Krone and Bitoshi offer possessions for the fallen, Quake says there is no fair bargain to be struck with Death. The exchange is refused. The full assault and its aftermath preserve the other companions’ appeals beside his refusal.

profile.personality: Quake is direct, forceful, and often willing to stand where uncertainty becomes action. His record shows both martial decisiveness and the ability to refuse a tempting solution when its moral price is hidden inside grief.
profile.achievements: He belongs to the first Calling, helps reopen Eovar’s route, organizes Pristinia, pursues the Compass crisis, helps build the walls, and uses the Gael crown to command ancient statues and reveal an escape. When Wrath offers restoration after Dale’s death, Quake refuses and creates space for another answer.
profile.relationships: Elenia later protects Quake because he previously saved Nienna and her, turning an earlier deed into a lasting obligation of care. Gartina, Jiangshi, Adelia, Saray, Wren, and Dale accompany many of his defining expeditions, while his refusal of Wrath links personal loyalty to the campaign’s wider rejection of coerced sacrifice.
